quarantine.definition: keeping someone apart because they may have been exposed to a disease.

reagent.definition: a chemical used in a test to find out what substance is present

recipient.definition: a person who receives blood from a donor

rectum.definition: the final part of the large intestine where waste is stored before leaving the body

red blood cell.definition: a blood cell that carries oxygen around the body

reducing sugar.definition: a sugar that can change Benedict’s solution from blue to other colours when heated

reflux.definition: the backward flow of stomach contents into the oesophagus

regurgitate.definition: to bring swallowed food back up to the mouth

regurgitation.definition: the return of swallowed food to the mouth for chewing again

rennin.definition: an enzyme that helps to curdle milk in the stomach

respiration.definition: the process in living things that releases energy from food

respiratory surface.definition: a body surface where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged

reticulum.definition: the second chamber of a ruminant stomach where food is mixed and softened

Rhesus factor.definition: a substance on red blood cells that makes blood Rh positive when present

rhizoid.definition: a root-like structure in some simple organisms that helps them attach and absorb nutrients

rib cage.definition: the bony structure in the chest that protects the heart and lungs

rickets.definition: a disease in children that makes bones soft and weak, often due to lack of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus

root hair.definition: a tiny extension of a root cell that absorbs water and mineral salts from the soil

root pressure.definition: the force in roots that pushes water and dissolved mineral salts upward through the xylem

roughage.definition: the indigestible fibre in plant food that helps food move through the gut

rumen.definition: the first and largest chamber of a ruminant stomach where food is stored and mixed with bacteria

ruminant.definition: an animal such as a cow or goat that chews food, swallows it, and later chews it again

saliva.definition: the liquid in the mouth that moistens food and begins digestion

saliva amylase.definition: an enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch in the mouth

salivary amylase.definition: an enzyme in saliva that breaks down cooked starch into maltose

salivary gland.definition: a gland in the mouth that produces saliva

saprophytic.definition: feeding on dead and decaying organic matter

saprophytic nutrition.definition: a type of nutrition in which an organism feeds on dead and decaying matter

sedentary.definition: spending a lot of time sitting and doing little physical activity

sedentary worker.definition: a person whose work involves sitting or staying in one place for long periods

semi-permeable membrane.definition: a thin layer that allows some substances, especially water, to pass through but blocks others

semilunar valve.definition: a valve at the base of the aorta or pulmonary artery that prevents blood from flowing backward.

septum.definition: the wall that separates the left and right sides of the heart.

serum.definition: the clear fluid left after blood has clotted

sickle-cell anaemia.definition: an inherited blood disorder in which red blood cells become sickle-shaped and carry less oxygen

sieve plate.definition: the perforated end wall between sieve tube cells that allows food to pass through

sieve tube.definition: a phloem tube made of joined cells that carries food through the plant

sinoatrial node.definition: a small group of cells in the heart that starts and controls the heartbeat.

small intestine.definition: the long part of the gut where most digestion and absorption take place

sodium bicarbonate.definition: a mild base used to reduce acidity in a mixture

sodium hydroxide.definition: a strong base used to neutralise acids in experiments

solute.definition: a substance that is dissolved in a liquid

solvent.definition: a liquid that dissolves another substance

specialised cells.definition: cells that have a particular structure and job in the plant body

sphincter.definition: a ring of muscle that opens and closes a passage in the body

sphygmomanometer.definition: an instrument used to measure blood pressure

spina bifida.definition: a birth condition in which the spine does not form completely

spleen.definition: an organ that helps remove old blood cells and supports body defense

spongy mesophyll.definition: the loose layer inside a leaf with many air spaces for gas exchange

starch.definition: a carbohydrate found in foods like maize, cassava, and potatoes

sternum.definition: the breastbone in the middle of the chest

stock solution.definition: a prepared solution kept in a container, from which a smaller amount is taken for experiments

stoma.definition: a tiny opening in a leaf that allows gases and water vapour to pass in and out

stomach.definition: a muscular organ where food is stored and mixed with digestive juices

stomata.definition: tiny openings on leaves that allow gases and water vapour to move in and out

stomatal transpiration.definition: loss of water through the stomata of leaves

stroke.definition: a condition that happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel in the brain bursts

substrate.definition: the material or surface on which an organism grows or acts

succus entericus.definition: intestinal juice made in the small intestine that contains enzymes for completing digestion

sucrase.definition: an enzyme that changes sucrose into glucose and fructose

sucrose.definition: common table sugar made from glucose and fructose

Sudan III.definition: a dye used to test for lipids by colouring the oil layer red

Sudan III test.definition: a food test used to detect fats and oils

surface area.definition: the total area of the outside of something; increasing it helps enzymes work faster

surface area to volume ratio.definition: the relationship between the outside area of an object and the space inside it; it affects how fast materials move in or out

suspension.definition: a mixture in which small particles are spread through a liquid without dissolving

symbiosis.definition: a close living relationship between two different organisms

symbiotic nutrition.definition: a feeding relationship between two different species living closely together, where one or both benefit

systemic circulation.definition: the movement of blood between the heart and the rest of the body, except the lungs

systole.definition: the stage of the heartbeat when the heart contracts and pumps blood out

systolic pressure.definition: the pressure in the arteries when the ventricles contract

T-helper cell.definition: a type of white blood cell that helps control the body’s immune response

tap root.definition: a single thick main root that grows deep into the soil

thoracic cavity.definition: the chest space that contains the lungs and heart

thorax.definition: the chest part of the body between the neck and the abdomen

thrombin.definition: a blood protein that helps change fibrinogen into fibrin during clotting

thromboplastin.definition: a substance that starts the blood clotting process after injury

tissue.definition: a group of similar cells working together to do a special job

tissue fluid.definition: fluid formed from blood plasma that surrounds body cells and helps exchange materials between blood and cells

toxin.definition: a harmful poison made by some living things such as bacteria

trachea.definition: the tube that carries air to and from the lungs

tracheal system.definition: a system of air tubes in insects used for breathing

tracheid.definition: a long, narrow dead xylem cell that helps transport water and also supports the plant

translocation.definition: the movement of manufactured food in plants from leaves to other parts of the plant

translucent.definition: allowing light to pass through, but not clearly enough to see details

transpiration.definition: the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through the leaves

transpiration pull.definition: the pulling force created when water evaporates from leaves, drawing more water up through the xylem

transpiration stream.definition: the continuous flow of water through the xylem from roots to leaves

transport.definition: the movement of materials from one place to another in an organism

tricuspid valve.definition: the valve between the right auricle and the right ventricle.

trypsin.definition: an enzyme that breaks down proteins in the small intestine

tuberculosis.definition: a serious infectious disease, usually affecting the lungs, caused by bacteria.

turgid.definition: swollen and firm because a plant cell has taken in water

ulcer.definition: a sore that forms on the lining of an organ, such as the stomach

unicellular organism.definition: a living thing made of only one cell

universal donor.definition: a person whose blood can be given to people of all ABO blood groups

universal recipient.definition: a person who can receive blood from all ABO blood groups

vaccination.definition: the act of giving a vaccine to protect against disease.

vacuole.definition: a space inside a cell that stores water, cell sap, and other materials

valve.definition: a flap-like structure that keeps blood flowing in one direction.

vascular bundle.definition: a group of transport tissues in a plant, usually made of xylem and phloem together

vascular cambium.definition: a layer of dividing cells in a stem that produces new xylem and phloem

vascular system.definition: the plant transport system made of tissues that carry water, mineral salts, and food to different parts of the plant

vein.definition: a line of vascular tissue in a leaf that carries water and food

vena cava.definition: the largest vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart.

ventricle.definition: a lower chamber of the heart that pumps blood out of the heart.

venule.definition: a very small vein that connects capillaries to veins

vessel element.definition: a xylem cell that joins with others end to end to form a tube for carrying water

villi.definition: small finger-like projections in the small intestine that increase absorption

villus.definition: a small finger-like projection in the small intestine that increases surface area for absorption

vitamin.definition: an organic nutrient needed in small amounts for normal growth and body functions

water potential.definition: a measure of how freely water can move in a solution

water vapour.definition: water in gas form in the air

water-soluble.definition: able to dissolve in water and not usually stored in the body

white blood cell.definition: a blood cell that helps the body fight disease and infection

whole grain.definition: grain food that keeps all its natural parts and is healthier than refined grain

xylem.definition: plant tissue that transports water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant

zinc.definition: a mineral needed for growth, healing, and a strong immune system
